benchmark_metadata.metric_scope_disclosure: Precision, recall, FPR, and FNR are scenario-level metrics evaluating whether CloudShield classifies each of the 7 test scenarios into the correct high-level verdict. They do NOT represent individual request-level packet inspection metrics.
benchmark_metadata.workload_validity_note: Workload validity strictly requires all configured scheduling slots to be dispatched and completed without backpressure or missed slots. A missed scheduling slot indicates the scheduler timer hit the immutable duration deadline before the final slot could be submitted (unattempted workload). This is strictly distinct from submitted requests that timed out or failed in worker threads, and distinct from Nginx HTTP 503 rejections (which represent completed HTTP transactions). Runs with any missed slots or backpressure remain marked RATE_LIMITED_OR_INCOMPLETE.
benchmark_metadata.ttd_measurement_caveat: Detection latency is reported via two distinct metrics: (1) time_to_first_alert_sec (legacy alias time_to_detect_sec) measuring elapsed time to the first non-NORMAL state, and (2) time_to_ground_truth_match_sec measuring elapsed time to the first observation matching the scenario ground-truth label. Resolution is limited by the 4.0s background evaluation loop in backend/app/main.py and 0.5s observer polling cadence. Observed TTD values are discrete measurements quantized to evaluation intervals (~4s, ~8s), not continuous line-rate detection latency.
benchmark_metadata.scaling_mode_disclosure: Tier 3 horizontal autoscaling executes as SIMULATED_LOCAL in local Docker environments without AWS credentials; no actual cloud instances or additional container replicas are provisioned unless live AWS ASG credentials are explicitly configured.
limitations_and_residual_state: Nginx access log telemetry uses a 10s sliding window; an 11s pause is enforced between scenarios.
EWMA baselines in entropy_engine evolve dynamically on normal traffic and are not hard-reset.
Docker Desktop on Windows NATs direct host connections to 172.28.0.1; simulation channel is required for synthetic source IPs.
Tier 3 horizontal autoscaling executes as SIMULATED_LOCAL in local Docker environments; no real cloud infrastructure expansion occurs.

metric_definitions.total_scheduling_slots: Number of temporal dispatch slots configured for the run: int(duration * target_rps).
metric_definitions.submitted_requests: Number of tasks successfully submitted to the executor before the dispatch deadline.
metric_definitions.completed_requests: Number of tasks whose futures genuinely finished. Includes successful responses and HTTP error status codes (403, 429, 503, 504). HTTP 503 is a completed HTTP request from Nginx or backend, NOT a worker error.
metric_definitions.worker_errors: Tasks that were submitted to the executor but terminated with an unhandled Python exception in the worker thread.
metric_definitions.worker_timeouts: Tasks that were submitted to the executor and were still active or pending when the drain deadline expired.
metric_definitions.unfinished_requests: Tasks submitted to the executor remaining unfinished (running or pending) after the drain timeout.
metric_definitions.cancelled_pending_requests: Submitted tasks that were successfully cancelled before starting execution in the worker thread.
metric_definitions.running_at_shutdown_requests: Submitted tasks that were already executing on worker threads (cancelling could not abort them).
metric_definitions.missed_scheduling_slots: Scheduling slots that were never submitted to the executor because the monotonic clock reached the scenario duration deadline or queue backpressure prevented timely submission. These represent UNATTEMPTED workload slots, strictly distinguished from submitted tasks that failed or timed out in worker threads.
metric_definitions.workload_delivery_distinction: A missed slot means the scheduler never attempted submission (e.g., dispatch loop ran out of time). In contrast, worker_errors, worker_timeouts, and unfinished_requests represent requests that WERE dispatched into the thread pool but failed to complete cleanly. HTTP-level error responses (e.g. 503 from Nginx or 403 from blocklists) are COMPLETED requests, not worker errors or missed slots.
metric_definitions.dispatch_window_rps: Rate of task submission measured strictly within the active dispatch window: (submitted_requests - 1) / dispatch_duration_sec.
metric_definitions.completed_request_throughput_rps: Genuinely completed tasks per second over the total run duration: completed_requests / total_completion_duration_sec. Excludes timeouts, errors, and synthetic records.
metric_definitions.dispatch_deadline_respected: True if no task was submitted at or after immutable_start + duration.
metric_definitions.workload_fully_delivered: True if all scheduled slots were submitted, completed without errors or timeouts, and no backpressure occurred.
metric_definitions.rate_limited_or_incomplete: True if backpressure, missed slots, worker errors, timeouts, or incomplete submissions prevented full workload delivery.
metric_definitions.runtime_bounding_note: Cancelling a future prevents queued pending tasks from starting, but cannot abort a worker thread that is already actively running. The drain timeout bounds the scheduler's wait time, not necessarily total Python process lifetime if threads remain running.
